application.name: ofetch
application.summary: The repository is a library (not an end-user application) built with unbuild and tested with vitest. Its core is `createFetch` in src/fetch.ts, which constructs the `$fetch`/`ofetch` callable implementing the full request pipeline: option merging, hook invocation, URL/query resolution, body serialization, timeout/abort handling, response content-type parsing, retry on failed responses, and normalized FetchError throwing. Two entry points export it: src/index.ts (uses global fetch) and src/node.ts (falls back to node-fetch-native with optional keep-alive agents).
application.purpose: A TypeScript fetch library providing an enhanced, universal HTTP client (`ofetch` / `$fetch`) built on top of the Fetch API, with automatic JSON handling, retries, timeouts, request/response hooks, base-URL/query handling, and normalized error objects.

Core factory producing the `$fetch`/`ofetch` callable; implements the entire request pipeline (option merging, hooks, URL resolution, body handling, timeout, parsing, retry-on-error) and exposes `.raw`, `.native`, and `.create`.
Retry-and-throw handler: on request or response error, applies retry policy (honoring retry counts, retry status codes, delays, and active aborts) and otherwise throws a normalized FetchError.
Node.js runtime adapter: returns node-fetch-native, optionally wrapped with HTTP/HTTPS keep-alive agents based on the FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable.

applicationFacts: Exports `ofetch` (aliased as `$fetch`) from both src/index.ts and src/node.ts, both built via createFetch.
`$fetch` exposes `.raw` (full response with parsed `_data`), `.native` (pass-through to native fetch), and `.create` (factory for instances with merged default options).
Request bodies that are JSON-serializable are auto-stringified with `application/json` content-type and accept headers set.
Response bodies are parsed based on Content-Type (json/text/blob/stream) using the `destr` library for safe JSON parsing; `parseResponse` can override the parser.

Retries: default 1 retry for non-payload methods, 0 for payload methods (PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE); retried status codes default to 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504; `retryDelay` supports fixed or callback-based delays.
Timeouts are implemented with AbortController, producing a TimeoutError-named error with DOMException code 23.
Lifecycle hooks are supported: onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError (each accepts a function or array of functions).
`ignoreResponseError` option returns error responses instead of throwing; null-body statuses (101, 204, 205, 304) and HEAD requests skip body parsing.
src/node.ts supports optional HTTP/HTTPS keep-alive agents via the FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable.
Tests spin up an h3 HTTP server via listhen with fixture routes (/ok, /params, /echo, /post, /binary, /403, /408, /204, /timeout) to exercise client behavior.
Build configuration (build.config.ts) emits declarations and CJS via unbuild for the src/index and src/node entry points.
